title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with RLHF
authors: Y. Bai, A. Jones, K. Ndousse, et al. (31 authors)
before: RLHF results came from one lab, with private data.
problem: Helpfulness and harmlessness pull against each other, and nobody had studied the tradeoff openly.
breakthrough: A full RLHF assistant study separating the two objectives, with the human preference dataset released.
why: It gave the open community real preference data and named the tension every assistant has to manage.
next: Constitutional AI replaced much of the human harmlessness labelling with AI feedback.
inherits: The helpfulness-harmlessness tradeoff, and open preference datasets.
